exploration.title: River Sculptor
exploration.subject: Earth science
exploration.summary: Compare vegetation and slope, then account for soil that stays, deposits or exits downstream.
exploration.question: How do vegetation and catchment slope change runoff and soil transport in this model?
exploration.explanation: Water erosion detaches and transports soil. Sediment can settle where flow slows or continue downstream. Vegetation and stable soil structure can increase infiltration and reduce runoff, while long, steep slopes can increase the power of water to erode and transport soil. This one-hour, one-hectare teaching model holds many real conditions fixed so you can compare one variable at a time. Its runoff, erosion, export and channel-capacity coefficients are invented; the results are not field measurements or a flood forecast.

experiments.title: Add vegetation
experiments.instruction: Predict what happens to runoff and soil export when vegetation changes from 0% to 100%. Compare one 40 mm storm on an 8% slope with the same 5,000 kg starting soil, area and duration.
experiments.observe: Compare runoff, infiltration, soil moved, deposition and export in both trials. Which changes explain the smaller or larger downstream export?

experiments.title: Steepen the slope
experiments.instruction: Predict whether runoff, soil moved or both change when catchment slope changes from 2% to 20%. Compare one storm with rain fixed at 40 mm, vegetation fixed at 40% and the same 5,000 kg starting soil, area and duration.
experiments.observe: Runoff stays fixed in this teaching formula while soil moved and export increase. Explain why this result describes the model relationship rather than every real catchment.

exploration.misconception: Erosion does not destroy soil. Removed material is transported, then deposits within the reach or exits downstream. Clearer water can still mean sediment settled elsewhere.
